messages.author: 9860719641632b58
messages.subject: Buffer dtype mismatch in pystan 2.5.0.0.
parts:
My model, which used to work fine, crashes at the end of the sampling process with the following message

Exception ValueError: "Buffer dtype mismatch, expected 'long' but got 'double'" in 'pystan._chains.get_kept_samples' ignored
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::domain_error'
  what():  mean(m): v has size 0, but must have a non-zero size

Any ideas how to fix this?
Thank you!

messages.author: 9860719641632b58
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Buffer dtype mismatch in pystan 2.5.0.0.
parts:
Hi Allen

sorry for being imprecise. In fact, this occurs when I try to call the sampling result as e.g. with print.

The first line of the above error message doesn't always appear. Though it says in  any case:

terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::domain_error'
  what():  mean(m): v has size 0, but must have a non-zero size

The error does not appear at all when my chain is very short.
Maybe this is a hint, that something goes wrong in a certain region of the parameter space, which is hardly sampled
from for a very short chain. However, I wouldn't know why that should be the case.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Buffer dtype mismatch in pystan 2.5.0.0.
parts:
I was just about to submit a bug report and did a few more tests that made me fix the problem.
The number I passed to the 'thin' argument of stan.sampling(...) was a floating point number (10.0) not an integer.

Seems like the error does not appear anymore now that I casted it from float to integer.
